name: Google Workspace Alert Center
description: Google Workspace Alert Center alerts: what kind of alert, who or what it names, and what Alert Center itself did about it. One feed for the gws:alerts sourcetype (Splunk Add-on for Google Workspace).
source: Google Workspace Alert Center API v1beta1 (Alert, AlertMetadata, MailPhishing and related resources); Splunk Add-on for Google Workspace source types reference; the Splunk Common Information Model Alerts data model

feed.label: Google Workspace Alert Center
feed.description: Google Workspace Alert Center alerts: one record per alert, covering its type, severity, workflow status and (for Gmail phishing alerts) the flagged message and Alert Center's own automated response.

create_time.label: Create time
create_time.description: When Alert Center created the alert record.

start_time.label: Start time
start_time.description: When the event that caused the alert began or was detected.

end_time.label: End time
end_time.description: When the event that caused the alert stopped being active; absent means the alert is still ongoing.

update_time.label: Update time
update_time.description: When the alert or its metadata was last updated.

customer_id.label: Customer id
customer_id.description: The Google Workspace customer account the alert belongs to.

etag.label: Etag
etag.description: An optimistic-concurrency token for the alert or its metadata; used to avoid overwriting a concurrent update, not a lookup key.

severity.label: Severity
severity.description: How severe Alert Center rates the alert.

cim_alert_kind.label: CIM alert kind
cim_alert_kind.description: The Alerts data model's own category for the record (alarm, alert, event, task, warning or unknown), computed by this environment's search-time field rather than read from the Alert Center payload.

alert_type.label: Alert type
alert_type.description: The specific kind of alert, for example Phishing reclassification; decides what the data object carries.

description.label: Description
description.description: A human-readable summary of the alert.

dest_type.label: Destination type
dest_type.description: What kind of object the alert's destination is, for example an account.

src_type.label: Source type
src_type.description: What kind of object the alert's actor is, for example a user.

message_recipient.label: Message recipient
message_recipient.description: The email address the flagged message was sent to.

user_name.label: User name
user_name.description: The display name of the user involved in the alert.

src.label: Source actor
src.description: The object that is the actor of the alert event.

src_ip.label: Source IP
src_ip.description: Presumed to carry the request address behind the alert, following the src/src_ip pairing this repo's own Reports sourcetypes use; not populated on the one seeded record so unconfirmed here.

src_user.label: Source user
src_user.description: Presumed to carry an actor account tied to the alert, paired with src by CIM convention; not populated on the one seeded record so unconfirmed here.

app.label: Reporting app
app.description: The system, service or application that generated the alert event, as the Alerts data model names it.

reporting_system.label: Reporting system
reporting_system.description: Alert Center's own identifier for the subsystem that reported the alert, for example Gmail phishing.

payload_type.label: Payload type
payload_type.description: The protobuf Any type URL naming the shape of the alert's data object, for example a MailPhishing payload.

system_action.label: System action
system_action.description: What Alert Center's own automation did to the flagged messages.

customer_domain.label: Customer domain
customer_domain.description: The customer's primary domain named by the alert's domain id.

malicious_sender.label: Malicious sender
malicious_sender.description: The From header of the message that triggered a Gmail phishing alert; attacker-controlled and trivially spoofed.

message_id.label: Message id
message_id.description: The flagged Gmail message's own id.

message_time.label: Message time
message_time.description: The date of the event related to the flagged email, for example when it was sent or reported.

message_body_hash.label: Message body hash
message_body_hash.description: An MD5 hash of the flagged message's body text.

message_subject_hash.label: Message subject hash
message_subject_hash.description: An MD5 hash of the flagged message's subject, when the message was user-reported.

attachment_hash.label: Attachment hash
attachment_hash.description: A SHA256 hash of one attachment or MIME part of the flagged message.

gws:alerts.description: Google Workspace Alert Center alerts as the Splunk Add-on for Google Workspace indexes them: the Alert resource JSON, plus the add-on's CIM Alerts field aliases.
gws:alerts.note: The one seeded record is a Gmail phishing alert (data type MailPhishing); record_types lists the Gmail-phishing-source alert types the alert_type concept documents, not the full Alert Center catalogue.

gws_alert_time_fields.text: One alert carries five timestamps: createTime (record created), startTime/endTime (the underlying event's window), updateTime (metadata last changed) and the flagged message's own date. They can differ by months; pick the one the question needs.

gws_alert_id_lookalikes.text: alertId, messageId and etag are all opaque strings of similar shape. Only alertId identifies the alert; messageId identifies one email inside it; etag is a concurrency token, not a key to pivot on.

gws_alert_index_time.text: props.conf's [gws:alerts] stanza sets DATETIME_CONFIG = NONE with no TIME_PREFIX, so _time is index time, not createTime. A time-bounded search can miss or misplace real events even though createTime is present in the JSON.
